breadcrumb: Appendix A: Prosperity Council Engagement Report
tldr: Appendix A documents stakeholder engagement feedback on Oregon's economic competitiveness. Key themes include: need for competitive tax incentives (CAT reform prioritized), streamlined permitting and regulatory systems, infrastructure investment (water, wastewater, energy), land-use law modernization, and integrated workforce development aligned with industry needs. Stakeholders emphasize addressing Portland's economic trajectory and structural barriers to workforce participation.

bullets.text: Stakeholders call for competitive incentives including Jobs Growth Tax Credit, expanded Enterprise Zones, and right-sized Strategic Investment Program; rural stakeholders note Opportunity Zones and New Markets Tax Credits have not effectively reached rural communities.

CAT reform proposals range from administrative fixes (Department of Revenue rule interpretation) to structural replacement (Business Activity Tax or Value-Added Tax); stakeholders note CAT compounds at multiple points in supply chains and disproportionately impacts small businesses.

Survey respondents call for comprehensive tax modernization through bipartisan task force; several propose low-rate broad-based sales tax paired with offsetting reductions in income and corporate taxes.

Stakeholders recommend one-stop permitting systems, transparent dashboards, digital permitting, guaranteed permitting timelines, and fast-track pathways for strategic industries; wetland and floodplain permitting cited as particularly slow.

CPP reform (pause, overhaul, or Cap and Invest replacement), RMA modernization, and agricultural labor regulation changes (overtime thresholds, OSHA heat rules, farmworker housing) proposed to reduce cost pressures.

Water and wastewater capacity identified as binding constraint on business expansion in smaller communities; energy infrastructure (generation, transmission) increasingly cited as constraint on industrial competitiveness.
Land-use system overhaul recommended; proposals include updating agricultural product definitions, reforming LUBA challenge rules, reevaluating EFU designations, and streamlining UGB expansions.

Stakeholders recommend expanding Career and Technical Education from middle school through community college; workforce agencies consolidation and interagency data-sharing mandates proposed to improve coordination.
Childcare affordability and availability, along with concerns about Paid Leave program, identified as barriers to workforce participation and retention.
1:1 apprenticeship ratio requirement described as bottleneck for public construction projects; stakeholders recommend 2:1 or 3:1 ratios modeled from other states.
